text: Top Thrill 2 is a launched roller coaster located at Cedar Point in Sandusky, Ohio, United States. It originally opened as Top Thrill Dragster in 2003, becoming the tallest and fastest roller coaster in the world and the first strata coaster, with a height of 420 feet (130 m) and a drop distance of 400 feet (120 m). The ride, an Accelerator Coaster model from Intamin designed by Werner Stengel, could accelerate from 0 to 120 mph (190 km/h) in 3.8 seconds and was themed to Top Fuel drag racing, featuring a launch track resembling a dragstrip. It surpassed Superman: The Escape in height and Dodonpa in speed, setting three world records upon opening, but these were later surpassed by Kingda Ka at Six Flags Great Adventure in May 2005, which reached 456 feet (139 m) in height, a 415-foot (126 m) drop, and a top speed of 128 mph (206 km/h). Despite this, Top Thrill Dragster consistently ranked among the world's top steel coasters. On August 15, 2021, a guest was struck in the head by a small metal L-shaped bracket, called a flag plate, that dislodged from a train while waiting in line, resulting in a severe injury described as a "serious accident." The Ohio Department of Agriculture (ODA) investigation in February 2022 found that half of the bolts securing the flag plate had dislodged, despite regular maintenance including a pre-accident inspection. The ride was closed indefinitely pending an investigation and redesign. In 2023, Cedar Point announced that Italian manufacturer Zamperla would redesign the ride, renaming it Top Thrill 2. The new version features a second 420-foot (130 m) vertical spike tower and replaces the original hydraulic launch system with a linear synchronous motor (LSM) launch system, using a triple-launch sequence—forward, backward, and forward again—to reach the original top speed of 120 mph (190 km/h). The track length increased from 2,800 to 3,422 feet (853 to 1,043 m), and the vertical spike was topped out in early December 2023. The ride reemerged on May 4, 2024, with a new, longer experience, but its inaugural season was cut short after only a week due to train issues requiring modifications. The ride reopened for the 2025 season and reclaimed the title of tallest roller coaster in the world following the permanent closure of Kingda Ka, though this record was later surpassed by Falcons Flight when it opened on December 31, 2024. The original design, which included five cars per train, was modified to four initially, with a fifth car added midseason, and the drag racing theming was replaced with a more general racing theme, similar to Formula One, featuring a "CP Racing" logo. The trains, now supplied by Zamperla and based on the Lightning model, hold 20 people per train and are decorated with a stylized "CP Racing" logo. Riders are prohibited from bringing loose items, and metal detectors are installed at the queue entrance. The ride uses LSM launch technology, which, while generating less instantaneous power than the original hydraulic system, allows for lighter trains with larger wheels to reduce cool-down time and maintenance. The launch sequence includes a forward launch to 74 mph (119 km/h), a backward launch to 101 mph (163 km/h), and a final forward launch to 120 mph (190 km/h), with magnetic braking fins used to slow the train if it fails to reach the top. On rare occasions, trains may roll back due to weather or wind, and in extreme cases, mechanics manually push trains down from the top. The original construction began in April 2002 with concrete foundation work, with vertical construction by Martin & Vleminckx starting in the fall, and the top hat element reached 420 feet (130 m) in December 2002, requiring two cranes up to 480 feet (150 m) tall, only four of which existed in the U.S. at the time. The official announcement of the ride occurred on January 9, 2003, with the goal of building "the tallest and fastest roller coaster on earth," reaching 420 feet (130 m) in height and accelerating to 120 mph (190 km/h) in 4 seconds. The structure was built by Intamin's subcontractor Stakotra, and Cedar Fair registered a trademark for "Top Thrill Dragster" in March 2003. The ride opened on May 1, 2003, with a media day on May 1, and officially opened three days later. It experienced several incidents, including a faulty valve in 2003, a detached launch cable in August 2016, and debris strikes in 2004, all contributing to downtime. During the 2017 season, it was temporarily renamed "Top Thrill Cubster" in a wager with Six Flags Great America. In 2020, timed boarding passes called "Access Passes" were used during the pandemic. The ride had accommodated 18 million riders over 19 seasons by the time of its 2021 closure. In September 2022, Cedar Point announced "Top Thrill Dragster, as you know it, is being retired," with plans for a "new and reimagined ride experience." A portion of the track near the station was dismantled in late 2022, and in January 2023, the park released the tagline "A New Formula For Thrills." Zamperla was selected to redesign the ride, with Adam Sandy noting the LSM system would increase reliability and allow for lighter trains. Tony Clark stated the goal was to "enhance the experience, make it more reliable." The ride officially reopened on May 4, 2024, but closed unexpectedly on May 12 for mechanical modifications. It remained closed through August 2024, with Cedar Point announcing it would not reopen for the remainder of the season but would continue work for a 2025 reopening. The train issues were resolved in the offseason, and Top Thrill 2 reopened for the 2025 season. The ride is now marketed as the "tallest and fastest triple launch strata coaster" by Cedar Point and as the "tallest and fastest triple launch coaster" by Zamperla. The original design was one of two strata coasters ever built, along with Kingda Ka, and both were designed by Intamin. Top Thrill Dragster was the second hydraulically launched roller coaster from Intamin after Xcelerator at Knott's Berry Farm. The track was painted red with white stripes, and supports were white on the launch and brake areas and yellow on the tower. The ride's launch area features a "Christmas tree" light, and a message is played before launch: "Keep arms down, head back, and hold on." After descending the 270-degree spiral, the train stops with magnetic brakes. The ride's height and speed remain unchanged at 420 feet (130 m) and 120 mph (190 km/h), though the track length and experience have been extended.

On August 7, 2016, the launch cable of Top Thrill Dragster became detached, causing the ride to be shut down. Two guests were evaluated at Cedar Point's first aid center and later returned to the park, while the ride underwent a thorough inspection and reopened two days later. On August 15, 2021, a serious accident occurred when a guest waiting in line was struck in the head by a small metal L-shaped bracket, known as a flag plate, which dislodged from a train as it approached the end of its run. The guest suffered a traumatic brain injury and was treated at a nearby hospital. Top Thrill Dragster was closed for the remainder of the season. An investigation by the Ohio Department of Agriculture (ODA), completed in February 2022, found that half of the bolts securing the flag plate had dislodged. The report confirmed that the ride had undergone regular maintenance, including an inspection the night before the accident, which determined the metal plate to be in "normal, working condition." The ODA found no evidence that Cedar Point violated state laws or that the park had reason to believe the ride was in an unsafe condition. To reopen the ride, Cedar Point would have needed to perform repairs, including replacing "different or improper grade" bolts and fixing damaged track sections. Instead, Cedar Point chose to hire Zamperla to create a new version of the ride, which opened as Top Thrill 2 in 2024. The injured guest's family sued Cedar Point in 2023, and a settlement with confidential terms was reached on April 13, 2024.
